guitar.modelsText: G&L Rampage (early) / Gibson Les Paul (signature model)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Cantrell is well documented playing a G&L Rampage in early Alice in Chains years, later closely associated with Gibson Les Paul (his own signature model).
guitar.notes: Original entry correct and well documented.

tone.target: dry down-tuned grunge riff with heavy fuzz-crunch bite
tone.profile: dry down-tuned grunge riff with heavy fuzz-crunch bite
tone.summary: A heavy, fuzz-driven signal chain utilizing a powerful distortion and an aggressive British amp model paired with a 4x12 cabinet to achieve thick, tight, buzzing low-end tones.
corrections: shift from mid-scooped to snarling mids
favor dry fuzz-crunch over smooth saturation

rig.name: Alice in Chains - Them Bones - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and excessive noise inherent in high-gain fuzz tones.
Provide the necessary aggressive fuzz-crunch bite and thick low end required for grunge riffs.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is a general fuzz, but its aggression helps achieve the desired 'buzzing' quality over smoother saturation.

blocks.purpose: Add mid-range punch and tighten the attack of the riff without losing the fuzz foundation.
blocks.gap: The OD 9 is used here as a secondary boost/mid-shaper, compensating for potential muddiness from the heavy fuzz stage.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the powerful, aggressive British stack sound (Plexi/Soldano) needed for high-gain rock.
blocks.gap: The UK 50 is chosen over UK SLP or UK 45 as it offers a robust mid-focus suitable for grunge's snarling tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic, powerful British cabinet tone and necessary low-end punch.
Aggressively boost the upper mids to achieve the 'snarling' quality and cut through the mix.
Used as a final tone shaping stage to ensure maximum signal integrity and punch.
blocks.gap: While not strictly necessary, using the Volume module helps control overall output level consistency in high-gain settings.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default IR for a more specific, high-gain 4x12 that better captures the aggressive Marshall/Plexi sound.

proposals.reason: The current IR is generic; a specific high-gain cab will enhance the Plexi/Soldano character.
proposals.expectedGain: More defined upper mids and tighter low end.
